compare.title: DBC Config Lab
compare.subtitle: The same traders, different launch rules. See who profits and who pays under each Meteora DBC config.
compare.caveat: Bots are modelled two ways: snipers that buy in the first seconds, and patient bots that wait until the fee drops. Bots reacting to other signals — price, volume, other wallets — are not modelled. After graduation, trading continues on the migrated DAMM v2 pool.

typical.name: Typical meme launch

slow-burn.name: Slow burn

patient-bots.description: No first-second snipers; bots instead wait for the fee to drop before buying.

stock-listing.name: Tokenized stock listing
stock-listing.description: A newly tokenized name with an outside price: thin human demand over half an hour, and traders who know that price trading the launch toward it.

scenarioControls.vestedTokensSold: The creator sells their vested tokens after graduation

launchpadEconomics.title: Launchpad economics — what real launchpads earn
launchpadEconomics.intro: Every top mainnet launchpad config, with what its launches actually produced. Partner income is the trading fees the launchpad keeps from one launch's bonding curve — median and top quarter across its sampled launches.
launchpadEconomics.matching: Showing {shown} of {total} matching launchpads (read from mainnet on {date}).
launchpadEconomics.curveOnly: Curve income is bonding-curve fees. After graduation a launchpad earns only from the liquidity position the program gives its fee wallet: none when it keeps no liquidity, and not measurable when its fee wallet no longer holds those positions. After-graduation figures count fees in the quote token only (claimed plus pending). Fees taken in the launched token are valued at the curve's average price. USDC launchpads are converted at 1 SOL = 150 USDC.
